Package de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.service.process

Class PlatformState

java.lang.Object
de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.service.process.PlatformState
@Service public class PlatformState extends Object
The read side of the platform for a BPMN diagram: a Spring bean named platformState through which a gateway condition asks about a resource's live state, so a process can branch on the real world without a service task and without knowing any repository. 

 <sequenceFlow sourceRef="check" targetRef="react">
   <conditionExpression xsi:type="tFormalExpression">
     ${platformState.telemetryState(resourceId, 'temperature') == 'ALARM'}
   </conditionExpression>
 </sequenceFlow>

The read twin of the inbound facade. Where PlatformGateway lets a process act on the platform, this lets it read — the same principle applies: every read runs under the system identity and is gated by that principal's resource READ permission, so what a diagram may see is a checked property of the platform's own identity, not an open back door.

Reading, not deciding. The bean answers questions of fact (is it online, is it in alarm, what was the last value); the branching logic itself stays in the diagram, and any real computation stays in Java. This is the line the whole Flowable work holds: BPMN describes order, waiting and responsibility, it does not compute.

Author:
peter haller

  • Method Details

    • resourceOnline

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public boolean resourceOnline(Long resourceId)
      Whether a resource is currently online. Only MQTT resources report presence; a resource that does not is reported offline.
      Parameters:
      resourceId - the resource to query
      Returns:
      true if the resource is an online MQTT resource
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if no resource has that id
      org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException - if the system principal may not read it

    • telemetryState

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public String telemetryState(Long resourceId, String datapoint)
      The aggregate telemetry state of a resource's data point: "ALARM" if any enabled rule on that data point is currently in alarm, otherwise "OK". A data point with no enabled rule is not in alarm, so it reads "OK" — the absence of a rule is deliberately not a third state, which keeps a gateway condition a simple == 'ALARM' comparison.
      Parameters:
      resourceId - the resource to query
      datapoint - the data point name
      Returns:
      "OK" or "ALARM"
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if no resource has that id
      org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException - if the system principal may not read it

    • latestValue

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public double latestValue(Long resourceId, String datapoint)
      The most recent numeric value reported for a resource's data point.

      This is loud on purpose: a gateway that reads a data point which never reported, or whose last value is not a number, is a misconfigured diagram, and failing the expression makes that visible at once rather than letting a silent default drive the branch the wrong way.

      Parameters:
      resourceId - the resource to query
      datapoint - the data point name
      Returns:
      the last value as a double
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if no resource has that id, or the data point has no numeric value yet
      org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException - if the system principal may not read it
